1.  2021-2022 CITY COUNCIL REDISTRICTING PROCESS UPDATE – F2M21-28

  Andrew WESTALL, Principal, Bear Demographics & Research provided the City Council
  with an update on the 2021-2022 City Council redistricting process which takes place after
  each decennial census. The presentation included information on the City’s demographic
  profile with the 2020 Census adjusted data, the interactive online mapping tool residents
  can use to propose City Council district boundaries, and the upcoming public input
  workshops. The presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  Opened/Closed Public Hearing: Mayor LEE opened the public hearing and, as there
  was no one present that wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. WESTALL discussed the
  population numbers adjusted to include state prisoner data, the use of American
  Community Survey method, the large Latino population in Western Alhambra and as it
  would affect the Fifth District, public outreach to Cantonese speakers, and population of
  undocumented or non-citizen residents.

3.  ACCEPT GRANT: AMERICAN LIBRARY  ASSOCIATON  FOR  COMMUNITY
  PROGRAMMING – F2M21-18, M2M21-138

  The Alhambra Civic Center Library applied for and received a $1,600 grant from the
  American Library Association’s NASA@MyLibrary Partnership to support a community
  program related to the James Webb Telescope. The Library would host three family
  targeted programs at local parks that would focus on space exploration and the James
  Webb Telescope from November 2021 to August 2022. The grant funds would be used to
  purchase books, supplies and other materials in support of the program.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accept $1,600 from the American Library Association’s
  NASA@MyLibrary Partnership; appropriate revenue and expenditure funds in the amount
  of $1,600; and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M21-138)

4.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL SERVICES FOR THE CITYWIDE ASSESSMENT
  AND IMPROVEMENT OF BUS STOPS AND BUS SHELTERS – F2M21-68, RFP2M21-
  19

  The City of Alhambra currently has a total of 166 bus stops, however only 27 of those
  stops have shelters. This project will develop and implement a comprehensive plan to
  improve bus stops throughout the City. The improvement of our existing facilities will
  promote multiple modes of clean transportation options including improved first mile/last
  mile access. As part of the City’s effort to increase public transportation ridership and
  improve multi-modal access to destinations for residents, workers, and visitors, this project
  will improve existing facilities for transit riders by replacing outdated transit related
  sidewalk furnishings with new bus shelters, benches, trash bins, and other associated
  multi-modal sidewalk furnishings at various locations throughout the City’s existing
  transportation routes.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON spoke regarding the East Main Corridor which
  is not served by the Alhambra Community Transit (ACT) Bus routes.

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY spoke to the need for shade structures and
  better seating on bus stops. He supported the RFP. Councilmember PÉREZ agreed with
  Mr. Maloney’s comments and referred to additional sites which needed bus stop
  improvements. She continued to speak to the need to support low income and people of
  color who use public transportation as well as suggested the City seek funding

10-25-21
   opportunities from Los Angeles County Metro. Mayor LEE also supported the RFP and
  reported on conditions of bus stops in the community.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of Request for Proposals for
  Professional Services for the Citywide Assessment and Improvement of Bus Stops and
  Bus Shelters with proposals due no later than 4:30 p.m. on December 6, 2021.

5.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: 2020 CONCRETE IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT – F2M20-
  74, C2M21-11, M2M21-139

  On February 22, 2021, the City Council awarded a contract to Gentry Brothers Inc. for the
  2020 Concrete Improvements Project in the amount of $437,260.20. Three change orders
  were issued in the amount of $54,713. The change orders were issued to replace a
  damaged concrete bus pad on Main Street and for additional damaged cross gutters, curb
  and gutter and concrete driveway aprons that were added as work progressed. The total
  cost of the project was $491,973.20. This project was inspected by staff and all work was
  completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications. As such, it would
  be appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as complete and instruct that the
  Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Gentry Bros Inc. for the 2020
  Concrete Improvements Project as complete in the amount of $491,973.20; directed the
  City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation;
  instructed the Finance Director to release the 5% retention 35 days from the date of
  recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M21-139)

9.  RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE CITY’S BOARDS AND
  COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY FOR
  CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO AB 361 – F2M20-33, R2M21-42

  During COVID, the City conducted meetings offering teleconferencing accessibility to
  members of the public, City Council, members of City boards and commissions, City staff
  and consultants. The executive orders authorizing such meetings lapsed on September
  30, 2021, replaced with legislation in the form of AB 361. AB 361 was signed into law by
  the Governor on September 16, 2021, which went into effect immediately as urgency
  legislation (codified under Government Code § 54953), and waived certain provisions of
  the Brown Act in order to allow local agencies to continue to meet remotely. Specifically,
  the bill allows remote teleconference flexibility, but only when there is a state of emergency
  that makes it unsafe to meet in person. The City already implemented the requirements of
  AB 361 for conducting public meetings and was in full compliance, thus there would be no
  change of the currently established procedures. The proposed Resolution would make
  the required findings under AB 361, and if adopted, it would allow the City to continue to
  offer teleconference accessibility for public meetings, to help mitigate the spread of
  COVID-19, as well as during other state-proclaimed emergencies, such as earthquakes
  or wildfires, where physical attendance may present a risk. The resolution also directed
  staff to agendize for Council consideration no less than every 30 days the need to continue
  to utilize teleconferenced meetings pursuant to AB 361.

10.  APPROVAL TO AMEND CONTRACT K2M21-325 FOR CONTINUED TEMPORARY
  ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FOR THE POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M21-18, M2M21-
  141

  On May 5, 2021, the City entered into an agreement with Olympic Staffing Services to
  provide the Police Department with necessary temporary administrative staffing support
  due to the absence and vacancy of a position within the department. The terms of contract
  K2M21-325 were such that services may not exceed $50,000 unless authorized by the
  City Council. The contract was nearing its $50,000 limit. It was anticipated that the Police
  Department would have a continued need for the services provided by Olympic Staffing
  Services for temporary administration staffing support and that the cost to do so would
  require a contract amendment and an additional appropriation of funds. This amendment
  requested an additional $35,100 for a new total contract not to exceed amount of $85,100.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final
  language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of
  Alhambra and Olympic Staffing Services (K2M21-325) to provide continued temporary
  administrative support to the Police Department for an additional amount not to exceed
  $35,100; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M21-141)

11.  RESOLUTION SUPPORTING THE VISION ZERO STRATEGY TO ACHIEVE ZERO
  TRAFFIC DEATHS AND SERIOUS INJURIES ON ALHAMBRA STREETS – F2M21-70,
  R2M21-39

  12
10-25-21
   Per Council’s direction, as part of the 2021-22 Strategic Plan, the Council requested
  prioritizing the safety, health, and security of its residents, businesses, employees and
  visitors through the implementation of a Vision Zero strategy. Vision Zero, which was
  implemented in numerous communities throughout the world, was dedicated to eliminating
  traffic fatalities and serious injuries and increasing safety, health, and mobility for all. The
  strategy focused on safety as the principal objective for a multimodal transportation
  system using a data-driven, multidisciplinary, and safety systems approach. By adopting
  the proposed Resolution, Alhambra would advance insight into street safety, evaluate and
  recommend modifications to conditions, standards and policies to improve roadway safety
  and balance the needs of space within the public right-of-way.

  Public Comment:  Lewis MCCAMMON spoke to safety improvements made on Valley
  Boulevard and those that needed to be made in the East Main Corridor. He supported the
  Resolution.

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY, Councilmember PÉREZ, and Mayor LEE
  supported the Vision Zero Strategy and the Resolution. Ms. LEE spoke to the need to
  support bicyclists and their needs.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M21-39 entitled: A
  Resolution of the Alhambra City Council supporting the Vision Zero strategy to achieve
  zero traffic deaths and serious injuries on Alhambra streets

12.  AUTHORIZING RESOLUTION FOR GRANT APPLICATION UNDER MEASURE A
  COMPETITIVE GRANT PROGRAM – F2M21-18, R2M21-43, M2M21-142

  The Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) was
  responsible for implementing and administering the Los Angeles County Safe, Clean
  Neighborhood Parks and Beaches Measure of 2016 (Measure A) which authorized
  dedicated local funding for park, recreation, and open space projects and their
  maintenance through an annual special tax on all taxable real property in the County.
  RPOSD accepted competitive grant program applications for projects including the
  renovation of regional recreation facilities and aquatic centers. Staff identified a
  park/aquatics project at Alhambra Park Pool. The deadline to apply for the RPOSD grant
  funds would be October 28, 2021.

  Discussion:  None.

13.  APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS TO COVER WATER DAMAGE AT THE CITY YARD
  PUBLIC WORKS BUILDING – F2M21-17, M2M21-143

  A water heater was replaced at the City Yard Public Works building by a licensed plumbing
  company. The morning after the installation it was discovered that the new water heater
  had failed and had been leaking throughout the night. The building suffered damage to
  the ceiling, flooring, locker room and workspace areas. The City received a settlement
  offer from the plumbing contractors insurance company and would like to move forward
  with making the repairs. This recommendation was submitted pursuant to Municipal Code
  Section 3.36.070(a), which allows for emergency purchases if there is breakdown in
  machinery or essential services that require immediate supplies, equipment, or services
  to protect public health, welfare, or safety.

  Discussion:  None.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) F2M21-7

Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff for their work on the Strategic Plan. She
further reported that large trucks were driving through Poplar despite Alhambra signage regarding
weight limits. She suggested working with the City of Los Angeles to post additional signage in
the Los Angeles side of Poplar regarding vehicle weight limits. She went on to discuss the need
to review traffic safety conditions around Alhambra schools. She also supported Item No. 4.

Councilmember MALONEY discussed the success of the Alhambra Pumpkin Run, and thanked
staff and Joanna Vargas for their work on the event. Councilmember PÉREZ also spoke to the
success of the Pumpkin Run and recognized all volunteers.

Ms. PÉREZ requested agendizing discussion of a resolution in support of Roe v. Wade and
women’s reproductive health decisions. She went on to speak in support of Planned Parenthood
in Alhambra and the unique services offered. Councilmembers Andrade-Stadler, Maloney, and
Maza supported the discussion. Mayor LEE stated that while she would support a discussion,
she had reservations supporting a resolution which would conflict with differing opinions in the
community at large. City Attorney MONTES stated that there was not unanimous consensus to
agendize future discussion, and so the request would appear on the next agenda under Council

 Communications at which time Council could again discuss agendizing discussion at another
meeting.

Ms. PÉREZ went on to discuss Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments regarding Poplar Blvd and
“Reimagined Poplar,” as well as the San Gabriel Valley Council of Government Measure M
application with Assistant City Manager GARCIA. She referred once again to the Pumpkin Run
and the success of the beer garden and live music. She suggested experimenting with integrating
such features more regularly in the Farmer’s Market in a new effort to bring lift to the downtown
area to help businesses thrive.

Councilmember MAZA discussed community concerns with recently passed SB9 and requested
agendizing a formal discussion at a later meeting. Councilmembers ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE,
and MALONEY supported the discussion. Councilmember PÉREZ supported discussion, but
expressed that she had many questions about limiting SB9 while still making things flexible for
Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) construction. She also referred to the historically racist use of
single-family zoning codes. City Attorney MONTES stated that there was unanimous consensus
to agendize future discussion briefing Council on SB9 as well as the actions of other local cities.

Mayor LEE also reported on the success of the Pumpkin Run and the family feeling in the
community. She also mentioned feedback from a community member who expressed gratitude
for the Rental Assistance provided by the City during the COVID-19 pandemic.
